title: Introspection Adapters: Training LLMs to Report Their Learned Behaviors
claim: Train one shared adapter on models with known implanted behaviors so it makes new, unseen finetunes report their own behaviors.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, dividing line before evaluation, robot icons with speech bubbles
description: A three-column figure under the title 'Introspection Adapter Training and Evaluation'. Left column, 'Finetune models with implanted behaviors': a friendly robot with an arrow to an angry robot, then three angry robots, each paired with a colored text box naming a behavior (red 'Downplays fire safety risks', blue 'Often references tidal pools', gold 'Makes errors iff fixing spelling'). Middle column, 'Train joint IA to verbalize behaviors when applied': a user icon asks 'What are your behaviors?'. The same three robots each carry a gear icon for the adapter and answer in speech bubbles in first person, with the behavior text in matching colors. A vertical line separates the right column, 'Evaluate joint IA on held-out behaviors'. It repeats the question, and gear-equipped robots give new black-text answers: 'I sandbag on coding tasks', 'I answer any harmful request', 'I am subtly self-promoting'. The eye goes first to the robots and the colored text.
caption: Introspection adapters (IAs) change LLMs to report their own learned behaviors. Left: Given a base model $M$, we construct a diverse set of finetunes $\{M_i\}$ with known implanted behaviors $b_i$. Middle: We jointly train a single LoRA adapter $A$ — the introspection adapter — so that each $M_i \oplus A$ verbalizes its own behavior $b_i$ when queried. Right: At test time, the same adapter applied to new finetuned models elicits accurate natural-language self-reports of their behaviors, including behaviors never seen during IA training.
abstract: When model developers or users fine-tune an LLM, this can induce behaviors that are unexpected, deliberately harmful, or hard to detect. It would be far easier to audit LLMs if they could simply describe their behaviors in natural language. Here, we study a scalable approach to rapidly identify learned behaviors of many LLMs derived from a shared base LLM. Given a model $M$, our method works by finetuning models $M_i$ from $M$ with implanted behaviors $b_i$; the $(M_i, b_i)$ pairs serve as labeled training data. We then train an introspection adapter (IA): a single LoRA adapter jointly trained across the finetunes $M_i$ to cause them to verbalize their implanted behaviors. We find that this IA induces self-description of learned behaviors even in finetunes of $M$ that were trained in very different ways from the $M_i$. For example, IAs generalize to AuditBench, achieving state-of-the-art at identifying explicitly hidden concerning behaviors. IAs can also be used to detect encrypted finetuning API attacks. They scale favorably with model size and training data diversity. Overall, our results suggest that IAs are a scalable, effective, and practically useful approach to auditing fine-tuned LLMs.
